text: Welcome to this short briefing on rooftop beekeeping. In the next few minutes I will explain how our rooftop apiary works and what you need to get started. We installed our very first hive on the roof of the city library in the spring of 2019.
We installed our very first hive on the roof of the city library in the spring of 2019. Since then the apiary has grown, as you can see on this slide. A colony changes a lot during the year.

A colony changes a lot during the year. At the height of the season, the queen can lay up to 2000 eggs a day. The chart shows how the population evolves month by month. Safety comes first, and the rules on this slide are not optional.

Safety comes first, and the rules on this slide are not optional. And if you do get stung, scrape the sting out with a fingernail. Never pinch it, because that pushes more venom in. Here is what the beginner kit costs.

Here is what the beginner kit costs. Good news, during your first year, the association lends you a smoker for free. Our current queen is a Buckfast queen. She came from a breeder in Brittany, and she is calm and very productive.
She came from a breeder in Brittany, and she is calm and very productive. We harvest once a year, in late August. Last year we collected about 42 kg of honey.
Last year we collected about 42 kg of honey. Thank you for watching. The next beginner session starts on the 3rd of October. We hope to see you on the roof.
